{"id":"theos.sh-cqo","title":"Prevent local test runs from OOMing by serializing heavy Vitest suites","description":"## Problem

Running the test suites in this repo can exhaust local memory because the heaviest Vitest suites are uncapped and duplicate expensive browser/dev-server harnesses.

### Evidence
- `package.json:11-14` exposes `test:run`, `test:integration`, and `test:visual`, with `test:visual` bound directly to `vitest run --config vitest.visual.config.ts`.
- `vitest.visual.config.ts:3-9` sets only `environment`, `include`, and timeouts. It does **not** cap workers or disable file parallelism, so Vitest defaults apply.
- Local runtime on this machine reports `availableParallelism = 8`, and Vitest 1.6.x defaults to `pool=threads` and `fileParallelism=true`, so multiple visual files can execute at once.
- Every visual spec launches its own Vite dev server and its own Puppeteer browser:
  - `tests/visual/surface-smoke.test.ts:55-61`
  - `tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts:30-37`
  - `tests/visual/landing-smoke.test.ts:13-24`
  - `tests/visual/a11y-route.test.ts:8-14`
  - `tests/visual/game-flow.test.ts:9-15`
- Two of those specs also hardcode the default Vite port (`http://localhost:3000/surface/`), which means parallel runs create redundant extra dev-server processes even when only one server is actually used:
  - `tests/visual/surface-smoke.test.ts:57-59`
  - `tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts:32-34`
- The integration suite is a secondary amplifier: `vitest.integration.config.ts:7-17` also lacks worker limits while several tests allocate canvases / renderer state and iterate many frames or seeds (`tests/integration/golden-frames.test.ts:10-25`, `tests/integration/effect-interactions.test.ts:10-24`, `tests/integration/shadow-3d.test.ts:11-25`).

## Outcome

Make local test execution memory-safe on developer machines without deleting coverage.

## Proposed fix

1. **Serialize the visual suite by default**
   - Update `vitest.visual.config.ts` to disable file parallelism and explicitly cap workers at 1.
   - Prefer a process pool that avoids duplicating thread heaps for browser-heavy specs.
2. **Share the visual harness instead of re-spawning it per file**
   - Move Vite dev-server startup and Puppeteer launch into shared setup/global teardown.
   - Reuse a single server/browser per visual run when safe, instead of five independent copies.
3. **Bound integration-suite concurrency**
   - Add explicit worker limits (or targeted serial execution) for `vitest.integration.config.ts`.
   - Split the most memory-intensive cases into a dedicated config/script if needed.
4. **Make the safe path the obvious path**
   - Update package scripts/docs so the default human workflow uses the bounded configs.
   - Document when to run single-file visual tests vs the whole suite.
5. **Prove the memory regression is fixed**
   - Capture peak RSS / process counts for visual + integration runs before and after.
   - Ensure the safe defaults run successfully on a normal 8-core dev machine without OOM.

## Risks / notes

- Serializing browser tests will increase wall-clock time; if needed, CI can shard at the job level instead of local per-file parallelism.
- Reusing one browser/server requires careful cleanup between specs to avoid cross-test pollution.

- `src/effects/base/text-mask.ts` — drawMaskCanvas, MASK_SCALE=4, stacked vs single layout, fontWeight from `gateParam(seed,'fontVariation','weight')`. Produces face cells + textDensity (3×3 neighbor count).

{"id":"theos.sh-fg3","title":"Fix PRNG determinism break in P3 feature-biased artifact placement","description":"## Bug

`src/surface-game/artifacts.ts:44–51` consumes PRNG draws conditionally:

    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      const feat = featureUVs[i];
      const u = feat ? feat.u : prng.nextFloat();
      const v = feat ? feat.v : prng.nextFloat();
      const radius = lerp(minR, maxR, prng.nextFloat()) * rScale;
      ...
    }

When a feature point is available the two `prng.nextFloat()` calls for `u`
and `v` are skipped. When it isn't, they are consumed. Every downstream draw
(`radius`, `offset`, `spikes`) then shifts in the PRNG stream depending on
which slots got feature points.

## Impact

Determinism invariant violation. For the same seed:
- If `backend` is omitted (fallback path), the non-feature artifacts consume
  2 draws for u/v and subsequent draws for radius/offset/spikes land at
  positions P, P+1, P+2 in the stream.
- If `backend` is provided and a feature point lands first, those 2 draws
  are skipped and radius/offset/spikes land at positions P-2, P-1, P.

Existing `artifacts.test.ts` (~line 116) only compares u/v, so this slips
past CI.

## Fix

Always draw u/v from the PRNG, overwrite with feature if present:

    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      const uRand = prng.nextFloat();
      const vRand = prng.nextFloat();
      const feat = featureUVs[i];
      const u = feat ? feat.u : uRand;
      const v = feat ? feat.v : vRand;
      const radius = lerp(minR, maxR, prng.nextFloat()) * rScale;
      ...
    }

## Acceptance

- Extend `artifacts.test.ts` with a determinism check that also compares
  `radius`, `offset`, `spikes` across (seed, backend) pairs for the same
  seed with different surface configurations.
- Existing 301/301 tests green.

{"id":"theos.sh-srr","title":"Upgrade geodesic integrator from RK2 midpoint to RK4 per spec","description":"## Gap

Spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-17-3d-artifacts-manifold-walking-design.md,
Walking section, C3) specifies RK4 integration of the geodesic equation.
Shipped implementation in src/surface-game/geodesic.ts uses the explicit
midpoint method (RK2) — two acceleration evaluations per substep, O(h^2)
local truncation error, versus RK4's four evaluations and O(h^4) error.

## Impact

Unit-speed preservation drifts. The existing test
`geodesic.test.ts` "approximately preserves the metric norm of the velocity
vector" tolerates |n1 - 1| < 0.02 over ds=0.1 with 8 substeps — a 2% drift
per 0.1 arc-length. Over long walks the player visibly decelerates mid-hill
and the "Riemannian feel" degrades. At the default tunable
`walk.geodesicSubsteps = 4` the drift is worse.

## Fix

Replace the midpoint step in `geodesicStep` with a standard RK4:

    for (let s = 0; s < substeps; s++) {
      const [aU1, aV1] = geodesicAccel(m, u, v, uDot, vDot);
      const [aU2, aV2] = geodesicAccel(m, u + h*0.5*uDot, v + h*0.5*vDot,
                                        uDot + h*0.5*aU1, vDot + h*0.5*aV1);
      const [aU3, aV3] = geodesicAccel(m, u + h*0.5*(uDot + h*0.5*aU1),
                                        v + h*0.5*(vDot + h*0.5*aV1),
                                        uDot + h*0.5*aU2, vDot + h*0.5*aV2);
      const [aU4, aV4] = geodesicAccel(m, u + h*(uDot + h*0.5*aU2),
                                        v + h*(vDot + h*0.5*aV2),
                                        uDot + h*aU3, vDot + h*aV3);
      u    += (h/6) * (uDot + 2*(uDot + h*0.5*aU1) + 2*(uDot + h*0.5*aU2) + (uDot + h*aU3));
      // etc. — use canonical RK4 formulation for coupled (position, velocity) ODE
    }

(Canonical form: treat (u, v, uDot, vDot) as a 4-vector, compute k1..k4 for
the full 4-vector derivative, then y ← y + (h/6)(k1 + 2k2 + 2k3 + k4).)

## Acceptance

- `geodesic.test.ts` metric-norm-preservation tolerance tightened to 0.005
  or better at ds=0.1, substeps=8.
- The C3 chord-length test in `player.test.ts` still passes.
- Existing 301/301 tests green.

{"id":"theos.sh-b26","title":"Fix phantom hit in marchTerrain coarse→fine transition","description":"## Bug

`src/renderer/ascii-raycast/march.ts:107` sets `prevD = stride` after a coarse
(sphere-trace) jump. `stride` is a positive distance-to-travel, not a signed
distance to the surface. On the next iteration that enters the fine band, the
crossing check at line ~123

  if (prevD > 0 && d <= 0) { ... }

fires on stale data — `prevD > 0` is trivially true because it's a stride
length, so the very first fine step after exiting coarse phase can spuriously
trigger a "crossing." The interpolated hit parameter `k = prevD / (prevD - d)`
ends up outside `[0, 1]` and the returned hit point is displaced from the
actual surface.

## Impact

Phantom hits on near-tangent rays — e.g. rays grazing the inner equator of the

{"id":"theos.sh-cqo","title":"Prevent local test runs from OOMing by serializing heavy Vitest suites","description":"## Problem

Running the test suites in this repo can exhaust local memory because the heaviest Vitest suites are uncapped and duplicate expensive browser/dev-server harnesses.

### Evidence
- `package.json:11-14` exposes `test:run`, `test:integration`, and `test:visual`, with `test:visual` bound directly to `vitest run --config vitest.visual.config.ts`.
- `vitest.visual.config.ts:3-9` sets only `environment`, `include`, and timeouts. It does **not** cap workers or disable file parallelism, so Vitest defaults apply.
- Local runtime on this machine reports `availableParallelism = 8`, and Vitest 1.6.x defaults to `pool=threads` and `fileParallelism=true`, so multiple visual files can execute at once.
- Every visual spec launches its own Vite dev server and its own Puppeteer browser:
  - `tests/visual/surface-smoke.test.ts:55-61`
  - `tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts:30-37`
  - `tests/visual/landing-smoke.test.ts:13-24`
  - `tests/visual/a11y-route.test.ts:8-14`
  - `tests/visual/game-flow.test.ts:9-15`
- Two of those specs also hardcode the default Vite port (`http://localhost:3000/surface/`), which means parallel runs create redundant extra dev-server processes even when only one server is actually used:
  - `tests/visual/surface-smoke.test.ts:57-59`
  - `tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts:32-34`
- The integration suite is a secondary amplifier: `vitest.integration.config.ts:7-17` also lacks worker limits while several tests allocate canvases / renderer state and iterate many frames or seeds (`tests/integration/golden-frames.test.ts:10-25`, `tests/integration/effect-interactions.test.ts:10-24`, `tests/integration/shadow-3d.test.ts:11-25`).

## Outcome

Make local test execution memory-safe on developer machines without deleting coverage.

## Proposed fix

1. **Serialize the visual suite by default**
   - Update `vitest.visual.config.ts` to disable file parallelism and explicitly cap workers at 1.
   - Prefer a process pool that avoids duplicating thread heaps for browser-heavy specs.
2. **Share the visual harness instead of re-spawning it per file**
   - Move Vite dev-server startup and Puppeteer launch into shared setup/global teardown.
   - Reuse a single server/browser per visual run when safe, instead of five independent copies.
3. **Bound integration-suite concurrency**
   - Add explicit worker limits (or targeted serial execution) for `vitest.integration.config.ts`.
   - Split the most memory-intensive cases into a dedicated config/script if needed.
4. **Make the safe path the obvious path**
   - Update package scripts/docs so the default human workflow uses the bounded configs.
   - Document when to run single-file visual tests vs the whole suite.
5. **Prove the memory regression is fixed**
   - Capture peak RSS / process counts for visual + integration runs before and after.
   - Ensure the safe defaults run successfully on a normal 8-core dev machine without OOM.

## Risks / notes

- Serializing browser tests will increase wall-clock time; if needed, CI can shard at the job level instead of local per-file parallelism.
- Reusing one browser/server requires careful cleanup between specs to avoid cross-test pollution.

{"id":"theos.sh-lf7","title":"Rework diegetic title to match legacy visual parity","description":"## Why

szv shipped a diegetic billboard (per-char spherical quad) but lost all visual richness of the legacy pre-diegetic title: big ASCII-art letters, shadow halo, seed-shuffled reveal, secondary-color density glyphs via charset-variant. User flagged: "current implementation lacks all features of the original."

Goal: rebuild title rendering to legacy parity while keeping the billboard diegetic (world-space, raycast-intersected, survives walk-away/return, works across seeds).

## Current state (post-szv, HEAD=8e835be)

- `HitKind = 'terrain' | 'artifact' | 'title' | 'sky'` in src/surface-game/types.ts
- src/renderer/ascii-raycast/title.ts: spherical billboard, per-char advance, per-char time-based reveal. Insufficient — looks like plain text on a floating sign.
- src/renderer/ascii-raycast/render.ts: accepts `title?, elapsedMs?`; picks nearest hit; emits `hitKind:'title'` with glyph from intersectTitle.
- src/surface-game/loop.ts: owns `title: TitleMarker`, accumulates `elapsedMs`, threads to renderFrame.
- src/effects/base/surface-cells.ts: title → face layer, accent×1.4, sat = sa*satAt. Uses charOverride.
- Tests: title.test.ts (6), render.test.ts (+2 title cases), surface-cells.test.ts (+2 title cases).
- Visual snapshot tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts pinned `f28c1c983ccb0476`.

## Legacy references (pre-diegetic, last seen at commit 84625b5)

Read these via `git show 84625b5:<path>`:

- `src/effects/base/text-mask.ts` — drawMaskCanvas, MASK_SCALE=4, stacked vs single layout, fontWeight from `gateParam(seed,'fontVariation','weight')`. Produces face cells + textDensity (3×3 neighbor count).
- `src/effects/base/text-cells.ts` — emits cells: secondary color, FADE_BAND=5, layer=3 (face) v=density/4, layer=1 (shadow) v=0.35 + density/4*0.25. No charOverride (charset-variant picks glyph).
- `src/effects/base/shadow-3d.ts` — projects layerMask=1 (face) along angle = `gateParam(seed,'shadow3D','angle')*2π` to produce shadow mask.
- `src/effects/base/reveal.ts` — REVEAL_TOTAL_MS=6000, shuffle by `(hCol ^ hRow) >>> 0` sort (hashes via sha256First32(concatBytes(seed, SEPARATOR, encode("reveal:col:"+N)))), count = round(total * (elapsed/6000)^1.5).
- `src/effects/base/charset-variant.ts` — 6 palettes, selected by `gate(seed,'charsetVariant')`; renderer: `palette[clampDensityIndex(cell.density)]`.
- `src/effects/base/manifold-genus.ts` — carves layerMask=-1 voids (optional; may skip for diegetic).
- `src/effects/base/text-distortion.ts` — sinusoidal col shift (optional; mask-space port or skip).

## Plan

### 1. Rewrite src/renderer/ascii-raycast/title.ts

```ts
interface TitleMarker {
  center: Vec3;
  text: string;               // 'theos.sh'
  widthWorld: number;
  heightWorld: number;
  // rasterized grids (MASK_SCALE=4, e.g. 256×32 -> 64×8 cells)
  maskW: number;
  maskH: number;
  alpha: Uint8Array;          // 0/255 per sub-pixel
  density: Uint8Array;        // 0..9 per face cell
  shadowMask: Uint8Array;     // 0/1 per cell
  revealOrder: Uint32Array;   // face indices in reveal order
  revealTotalMs: number;      // 6000
}

interface TitleHit {
  distance: number;
  kind: 'face' | 'shadow';
  density: number;
  maskIdx: number;
}

createTitleMarker(t: TunablesShape, seed: Uint8Array): TitleMarker
  // 1. Canvas rasterize text with gateParam(seed,'fontVariation','weight')
  // 2. Build density via 3×3 neighbor count over alpha
  // 3. Build shadowMask via projection along gateParam(seed,'shadow3D','angle')
  // 4. Build revealOrder: sort face cell indices by (hashCol(seed,col) ^ hashRow(seed,row)) >>> 0

intersectTitle(ray, marker, playerPos, elapsedMs): TitleHit | null
  // ray-plane intersect billboard; compute (localU,localV); sample mask
  // gate by reveal count = round(face.length * (elapsedMs/revealTotalMs)^1.5)
  // face hits only if maskIdx within revealed prefix; shadow hits always (or gate separately?)
```

### 2. Add `'title-shadow'` to HitKind

src/surface-game/types.ts — extend union. ShadedCell for title-shadow carries density via luminance.

### 3. Update render.ts

Emit `hitKind: 'title'` (face) or `'title-shadow'` with luminance=density/9, glyph=' ' (charset-variant picks). Keep nearest-hit arbitration.

### 4. Rework src/effects/base/surface-cells.ts title handler

- Use `scheme.secondary` (not accent).
- Face: `cell.value = density / 4; cell.saturation = sa * satAt; cell.layer = 'face';` NO charOverride — let charset-variant palette pick from density.
- Shadow: `cell.value = 0.35 + density * 0.25; cell.layer = 'shadow';` NO charOverride.
- Register charset-variant (or equivalent density-indexed palette) in WALK_SCENE_EFFECTS so title glyphs look right.

### 5. loop.ts / createGame

Pass `seed` into createTitleMarker. Keep elapsedMs accumulation.

### 6. Tests

- title.test.ts: rasterization sanity (alpha non-empty, density bounded), shuffled-reveal determinism (same seed → same order), reveal-count easing, hit kinds (face/shadow), billboard geometry unchanged.
- render.test.ts: title-face AND title-shadow cells visible at pitch=1.3, late-time; reveal gate keeps early face count < late face count.
- surface-cells.test.ts: face uses secondary-tinted HSV + density/4; shadow layer uses 0.35+density*0.25; no charOverride.
- Visual: re-run tests/visual/surface-walk-effects.test.ts, update snapshot hash once rework lands.

## Acceptance

- Title visible across ≥3 seeds with legacy-feeling richness (big letters, halo, seed-variant glyphs).
- Saturation field still modulates title (carry forward from szv).
- Shuffled reveal completes within 6000ms, deterministic per seed.
- Shadow halo renders with secondary color at lower value than face.
- Survives walk-away + return (billboard persists in world).
- surface-smoke + surface-walk-effects green (update hashes if intentional).
- typecheck green (no new errors vs main baseline).

## Risks

- charset-variant effect may not exist in current WALK_SCENE_EFFECTS — may need to port from 84625b5 or add density-indexed glyph selection inline in surface-cells.
- shadow-3d angle projection was screen-space in legacy — needs reformulation in mask-space or billboard-local space.

{"id":"theos.sh-8xq","title":"Upgrade artifact placement from P1 (random uniform) to P3 (terrain-feature biased)","description":"P1 ships first: seed deterministically picks N artifact positions (u_i, v_i) uniformly in the unit square, with N a small constant (3–7). {"id":"theos.sh-bsf","title":"Upgrade periodic noise from N2 (4D projection) to N1 (tunable Fourier spectrum)","description":"N2 ships first: h(u,v) sampled from 4D simplex noise at (cos 2πu, sin 2πu, cos 2πv, sin 2πv). Exact periodicity, natural-landscape look, seed → noise permutation table.

{"id":"theos.sh-je7","title":"marchTerrain signed-distance is not a true SDF far from surface","description":"Current signedDistanceToSurface in src/renderer/ascii-raycast/march.ts projects a ℝ³ point onto the bumpy torus via nearest-(u,v) inversion of the base-torus parametrization, then dots (p - φ(u,v)) with n̂(u,v). This is correct *near* the surface (small amplitude A, points within a few tube-widths) but becomes a poor distance estimate far away: (u,v) returned by atan2-based inversion is the nearest point on the *base* torus, not on the bumpy one, and the projection can jump discontinuously across the torus hole.

Symptom risk: marching rays that start far from the surface (large pitch offsets, distant eyes) may step past the real surface or report false-positive crossings.

Fix: replace with a proper SDF — either (a) analytic torus SDF + bounded amplitude correction, or (b) bisection-style inversion seeded from the ray origin's ring coordinates, or (c) sphere-tracing with a conservative Lipschitz bound. Option (a) is probably cheapest.

Gated on: we have not yet observed this in practice because eye lives on the surface. File for when we give the player fly mode or far-camera debug view.","status":"open","priority":4,"issue_type":"task","owner":"nyxhaile@proton.me","created_at":"2026-04-18T00:12:40Z","created_by":"Nyx","updated_at":"2026-04-18T00:12:40Z","dependency_count":0,"dependent_count":0,"comment_count":0}
